scope: Primary-source checks for seven new references; not a re-verification of every existing cited work.

sources.read_scope: Publisher-deposited abstract and bibliographic metadata, not the complete article.
sources.supported_claim: Base rates and false alarms constrain the posterior probability that an intrusion alarm identifies an intrusion.
sources.manuscript_use: Section 2.4: motivation for examining false-positive behavior for rare events; does not attribute the study's 1% ceiling to the paper.

sources.read_scope: Introduction and Section 4.3, Finite Mixtures, in the complete article copy hosted by MIT.
sources.supported_claim: Finite-mixture EM uses unobserved component indicators, conditional membership probabilities and weighted parameter updates.
sources.manuscript_use: Section 2.6: statistical foundation for mixture estimation; no claim that convergence validates drift detection.
sources.metadata_note: The modern publisher-deposited article record is pages 1–22. The archived scan is pages 1–38 including the discussion and authors' reply. The reference uses the article range, not the combined discussion range.

sources.read_scope: Author manuscript title, abstract, introduction and Section 2; accepted-paper version 3 dated 4 January 2019.
sources.locator: Pages 1–2, 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2019'
sources.supported_claim: AdamW decouples weight decay from the gradient-based optimization update.
sources.manuscript_use: Section 3.6: attribution for the optimizer already specified and used; no training settings changed.

sources.read_scope: NDSS publisher identity, complete-paper abstract and introduction.
sources.locator: Printed page 1; DOI in first-page footer
sources.supported_claim: Popularity-ranking composition, stability, representativeness and susceptibility to manipulation matter to security measurements; popularity is not a verified benign label.
sources.manuscript_use: Sections 2.3 and 5.3: rationale for treating Tranco as label-free control evidence rather than certified negatives.
sources.identity_note: First author is Victor Le Pochat. Publisher and paper author lists are used rather than inferred initials.

sources.read_scope: PMLR citation metadata and complete-paper abstract/introduction.
sources.locator: Printed page 3122; label-shift factorization and contrast with covariate shift
sources.supported_claim: Label shift changes P(Y) while preserving P(X|Y); the authors propose black-box shift estimation and correction.
sources.manuscript_use: Section 2.4: distinguishes fixed-rate prevalence projections from estimated deployment prevalence or implemented shift correction. Holding class-conditional rates fixed is narrower than asserting that every aspect of P(X|Y) has been verified unchanged.

sources.read_scope: Publisher-deposited metadata and extended author-institution abstract, not the complete article.
sources.locator: Google Research abstract beginning 'Systems that respond to user actions very quickly'; CACM 56(2), 74–80
sources.supported_claim: Latency variability and the slow tail matter to the responsiveness of large interactive services.
sources.manuscript_use: Section 2.9: motivates explicit tail-latency measurement, without claiming a scale match, diagnosing this study's exact mechanism or borrowing its numerical latency target.

sources.read_scope: USENIX publisher metadata and complete-paper abstract/introduction.
sources.locator: Printed pages 239–240, open/closed workload definitions and Figure 1
sources.supported_claim: Closed workloads make arrivals depend on completion; open workloads generate arrivals independently. This distinction affects latency and scheduling behavior.
sources.manuscript_use: Sections 2.9 and 3.12: interpret the existing fixed-concurrency harness and avoid converting closed-loop throughput into an externally imposed arrival-rate capacity claim.

not_added.reason: Metadata located, but existing Gneiting–Raftery coverage already supports the scoring-rule discussion; an extra foundational entry was not needed for this bounded pass.

existing_reference_reused: Schwarz (1978) is now also cited at the point where BIC selection is specified in Section 3.9.
retrieval_limits: Blocked publisher/OpenReview requests, a missing author PDF and one rate-limited request are preserved in retrieval logs. Alternate authorized public copies or publisher abstracts support the stated bounded claims.
